controls.label: Color + brightness
controls.qualification: The star's color, darker where TESS saw it dimmer (contrast drawn stronger) · April and May 2019, mapped in this project
controls.notes: YSES 1 in its own color, darker where its light in TESS's images of April and May 2019 says it was darker. As the star turned once in 5.46 days its light rose and fell by 5.3%. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the eye can see it: the darkest part gives 20.7% less light than the brightest, and is drawn as a much darker tone of the star's own hue; the Brightness map's scale has the measured values. The longitudes of the darker and brighter parts are measured. Their latitudes and shapes are not: they are the smoothest that reproduce the light. No change of color is drawn, because none is measured. Spots come and go within weeks or months: this is the star then. The darkening toward the edge is the Color dataset's limb law, drawn 1.5 times as strong.

controls.label: Brightness map
controls.qualification: Mapped in this project · TESS mission light curve, sector 11
controls.notes: Where the star's surface was darker and brighter in TESS sector 11, worked out in this project from how its light rose and fell by 5.3% as it turned once in 5.46 days. The light curve is the mission's own; Colman et al. (2024, AJ 167, 189) found the star's rotation in it, and starry finds the map that reproduces it at their period. The longitudes of the dark and bright regions are fixed by the data; their latitudes are not. No tilt of this star's axis is known: the map is made at 60°, the middle tilt of axes that point at random.
controls.legendNote: Darker: dimmer than the star's mean surface; white: brighter.

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color of Gaia's spectrum of the star. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of Gaia DR3's own spectrum of the star, from 380 to 780 nm. No image of its surface exists, and no darkening toward the edge is drawn.

physical.credit: Published or catalogue radius at the Gaia distance; Gaia DR3 astrometry; no measured rotation axis (display convention)
